content: 1. Calcium carbonate reduces the levels of strontium ranelate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 2. Streptomycin decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 3. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of sulfasalazine due to passive renal tubular reabsorption caused by increased pH. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 4. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses but decrease at higher doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. This interaction requires close monitoring. 5. Tafenoquine increases the levels or effects of famotidine by inhibiting organic cation transporter-2 (OCT2) and multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) transporters in vitro. Co-administration with OCT2 or MATE substrates should be avoided. If unavoidable, monitor for substrate-related toxicities and consider dosage adjustments based on the co-administered drug's labeling. 6. Teriparatide increases the levels of calcium carbonate through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administered, separate by at least 2 hours. 8. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of tiludronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by at least 30 minutes. 9. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of timolol by an unspecified interaction mechanism, likely involving inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 10. Tobramycin decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Torsemide decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide and calcium carbonate by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 12. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of trandolapril by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by increasing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 14. Triamterene increases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by decreasing renal clearance and decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 15. Trilaciclib decreases the levels or effects of famotidine by inhibiting OCT2, MATE1, and MATE-2K transporters. Co-administration with substrates of these transporters should be avoided, especially in cases where even minimal increases in substrate concentration could lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor closely for toxicities and adjust substrate dosage as needed. 16. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of ursodiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of vadadustat by drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Vadadustat may increase the exposure of OAT3 substrates. Monitor for adverse effects of OAT3 substrates and adjust substrate dosage according to their product labeling. 18. Famotidine and vandetanib may increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Famotidine increases the levels or effects of varenicline by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of verapamil through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of vismodegib by altering its solubility due to increased gastric pH, thereby reducing its bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of vismodegib by altering its solubility due to increased gastric pH, thereby reducing its bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of vismodegib by altering its solubility due to increased gastric pH, thereby reducing its bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Vitamin D increases the levels of magnesium hydroxide, particularly in the presence of renal impairment. The combined use of vitamin D and magnesium-containing products should be avoided in patients with chronic renal failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Calcium carbonate and willow bark interact through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses but decrease at higher doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 26. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of zoledronic acid by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by at least 30 minutes. 27. Patients with renal or hepatic impairment should exercise caution when using these medications. Dosage adjustments may be necessary. Prolonged QT intervals and torsades de pointes have been reported in patients with renal impairment. Relief of symptoms does not rule out the presence of gastric malignancy. 28. Pediatric patients may have an increased risk of developing acute gastroenteritis and community-acquired pneumonia. Some dosage forms may contain benzyl alcohol or sodium benzoate/benzoic acid, which have been associated with gasping syndrome in neonates. 29. Patients experiencing heartburn with symptoms such as shortness of breath, sweating, chest pain, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, unexplained weight loss, or pain radiating to the arms, neck, or shoulders should consult a healthcare professional. Discontinue use if heartburn persists or worsens after 14 days of treatment. 30. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk, making these medications generally acceptable for use during pregnancy.
